evidence.note: Systematic up-front reading of RFC 8878 in large contiguous ranges covering all major subsystems (frame headers, blocks, literals, sequences, FSE/entropy) plus targeted greps for tricky areas (Content_Checksum/XXH, FSE Table/Appendix A) and re-reads of narrow ranges (205-244 magic, 1204-1285) — all before coding starts at step 26.

Cross-checks understanding against real inputs by hex-dumping the first 64 bytes of four sample .zst frames (repetitive, audio, img, simple) with xxd and od — real byte-layout reconnaissance grounding the frame-header implementation.
Targeted spec lookups for specific tricky mechanisms (checksum/XXH, and re-reading the 1204-1285 range) show extraction of exact rules rather than reliance on assumed knowledge.

Deep entropy/sequence subsystems (audio/video frames) were resolved through a long trial-and-error edit/make/run loop with source re-reads but little further RFC re-consultation or byte-level cross-checking of FSE/Huffman internals — indicating the tricky-area model was not fully verified against real bytes before implementation, keeping this below anchor 8.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it read the RFC systematically section-by-section up front and inspected multiple real .zst frames with hex dumps before trusting its frame-parsing code. It falls short of a clean 8/10 because the demonstrated byte-level cross-checking is limited to frame headers, the hardest subsystems (FSE table build, sequences) were debugged via extensive iterative patching rather than verified against spec-plus-bytes beforehand, and no bit-level contract documentation is observable. That combination of strong, comprehensive orientation reading with partial (header-only) real-frame verification lands at 7.
